jobs.title: Director of Development for the College of Business
jobs.description:
Job Summary

Under the general direction of the Executive Director of Development, the Director of Development for the College of Business develops and executes strategies to secure philanthropic support for San José State University fundraising priorities identified by the University’s leadership in collaboration with the Office of Development in the Division of University Advancement. Responsibilities include but are not limited to identifying, qualifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding individuals capable of giving major gifts to the University. In support of these efforts, the Director of Development initiates, maintains and strengthens close working relationships with key academic leaders, campus administrators, various stakeholders, and University Advancement colleague.

Key Responsibilities

Manage an assigned prospect portfolio of key individuals supporting university fundraising priorities
Coordinate with Prospect Research Team to expand and enhance a prospect pipeline that aligns with university and campaign priorities
Actively manage a prospect / donor portfolio with annual goals for personal visits and fundraising outcomes based on established metrics
Develop and execute sound strategies to identify, cultivate, solicit and steward major gift prospects/donors – initiate contact, develop appropriate cultivation plans, and move individuals in an appropriate and timely fashion toward solicitation and closure
Present and regularly review top prospect strategies and immediate supervisor and other key team members as appropriate
Work collaboratively with the leadership of colleges, key university administrators and other stakeholders, offering them counsel on donor-centric cultivation and solicitation strategy, as appropriate
Work collaboratively with peers in Major Gifts as well as colleagues in Annual Giving, Planned giving and Corporate and Foundation Relations
Work with volunteer leadership providing them with direction and support in maximizing the college’s major gift fundraising potential
Focus on securing funding for designated priorities including research projects, innovation programs, scholarships, unrestricted support, facility renovations, new facilities and other specified priorities
Collaborate with stewardship colleagues with donor stewardship efforts particularly pertaining to the Division of Research and Innovation and help promote a culture of gratitude among internal and external constituents
Effectively utilize campus data management system and enter prospect/donor contact reports and their relevant data in a timely fashion
Prepare written donor cultivation and solicitation plans and proposals
Participate in staff, functional and strategy meetings including prospect review sessions, attend conferences, seminars, and other development training as feasible and appropriate

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Ability to identify donors and close gifts of six and seven figures
Ability to navigate the institution/assigned unit and make the appropriate match for donor interests
Ability to engage and support volunteer leadership with their efforts in fundraising, consultation, and advocacy
Skilled in networking and opening doors as well as developing donor-centric cultivation and solicitation strategies
Deep appreciation and understanding of the academic enterprise and the ability to articulate academic values internally and externally
Knowledge of clear, audience-appropriate communication practices for students, faculty, and staff, while maintaining a student-centered approach
Excellent oral and written communication skills
Ability to work as part of a collaborative team
Unquestionable integrity and commitment to professional ethics
High level of initiative, attention to detail, and organization skills
Ability to responsibly handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion
Skilled in successfully managing multiple projects on tight deadlines and under pressure in a dynamic and open environment
Ability to define problems, gather data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions
Proficient in Google Suite and Microsoft Office Suite and ability to utilize fundraising database programs, and learn new tech platforms for project management
Demonstrated spirit of flexibility and strong customer service ethic
Ability to interact with individuals from diverse backgrounds
Ability to responsibly handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion
Excellent customer service and public relation skills
Ability to communicate with constituents in a professional and respectful manner

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited institution
Three years of progressively responsible experience in fundraising
Experience developing donor centric solicitation strategies leading to closing major gifts
Evidence of strong written communication skills; ability to write clearly and persuasively

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced Degree
Experience developing donor (or client)-centric solicitation strategies leading to closing major gifts (or accounts)
Fundraising experience in capital or comprehensive campaign setting, preferably at an institution of higher education
Experience engaging and supporting volunteer leadership in their fundraising efforts

Classification: Administrator II

jobs.title: Associate or Full Professor of Environmental Science and Policy and Program Director, Tenured, Augus
jobs.description:
Description

Chapman University invites applications for an Associate or Full Professor of Environmental Science & Policy and Program Director in the Schmid College of Science and Technology starting August 2027. This is a full-time, tenured position that requires work to be performed in the State of California with specific in-person teaching responsibilities and required on-campus availability at Chapman's Orange campus.

Chapman University is a nationally ranked R2 institution offering traditional undergraduate and graduate programs in the heart of Orange County, one of Southern California's most diverse and vibrant regions. Our faculty are academic leaders who excel in both research and teaching. Dedicated to forward-looking, personalized education, we create an environment for unlimited achievement by both our students and faculty. More information about Chapman University is available at www.chapman.edu.

The Environmental Science & Policy Program is uniquely seated within two colleges at Chapman University: the Schmid College of Science and Technology and the Wilkinson College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences. Schmid and Wilkinson Colleges embody Chapman's mission of providing students with personalized educational experiences by fostering an outstanding community of teacher-scholars across a broad range of undergraduate and graduate programs. Schmid College has a new 140,000 sq ft home, the Keck Center for Science and Engineering. More information about Schmid and Wilkinson Colleges is available at www.chapman.edu/science
and www.chapman.edu/wilkinson
, respectively.

The undergraduate-only serving Environmental Science & Policy Program is home to a diverse group of faculty with interdisciplinary specializations across the breadth of environmental sciences (ecology, engineering, hydrology, remote sensing) and environmental studies (anthropology, environmental justice, natural resource governance, political science, sociology). The program serves the interdisciplinary Environmental Science & Policy B.S. degree, the Environmental Science minor, and the Environmental Studies minor.

We seek candidates with an active research program in areas including but not limited to:

Environmental health
Environmental toxicology
Water, soil, and/or air quality
Environmental contaminants
Natural resource governance

We value candidates who can identify avenues for collaboration both within and outside of the institution.

Faculty Role Responsibilities

The successful candidate will teach lower- and upper-level courses that contribute to the major and minors within the Environmental Science & Policy Program, maintain an active research program, and advise/mentor undergraduate research students. Significant scholarship, including publishing in peer-reviewed journals, presenting at relevant research conferences, and obtaining and managing extramural grants is an expectation of the position.

Required Responsibilities Include:

Teach lower- and upper-division Environmental Science & Policy courses, including core and elective courses. Current course descriptions are available at https://catalog.chapman.edu.
Continue a research program in interdisciplinary environmental sciences, including publishing papers and presenting work in this area at local and national conferences.
Actively contribute as an integral member of the Schmid College of Science and Technology in the ongoing development, implementation, and assessment of their academic and degree programs.
Perform service to the unit, college, university, profession, and wider community as expected of a tenured faculty member.

Program Director Responsibilities

The successful candidate will lead the Environmental Science & Policy faculty and degree program as Program Director for a minimum of three years in an at-will, compensated appointment separate from their faculty role.

Required Responsibilities Include:

Provide leadership, vision, and a voice for affiliated faculty, students, and degree programs.
Oversee program budget and advocate on behalf of the program for resource use.
Lead curriculum alignment and revisions, assessment reports, and course scheduling for the program.
Coordinate and participate in program and college events, including events for student recruitment and commencement, as appropriate.
Assign faculty to courses and hire appropriate part-time lecturers where needed.
Facilitate communication and collaboration between Schmid and Wilkinson Colleges pertaining to the support of this interdisciplinary program.

Qualifications

An earned Ph.D. in one of the environmental sciences (e.g., Biology, Chemistry, Environmental Science & Management) or related field by the start of employment from an accredited institution.
Earned tenure at the current institution of employment or equivalent.
A strong history of interdisciplinary environmental science research, including evidence of an independent, nationally recognized, externally funded research program.
Evidence of effective teaching at the undergraduate level, particularly in experiential learning courses, such as a senior capstone course, or upper division coursework.
Experience in curriculum development and learning outcome assessment.
Experience in leadership or administrative roles in academic service settings, such as college governance, curriculum, or assessment committees, ideally connected to interdisciplinary endeavors.

Application Instructions

Qualified Candidates Should Submit The Following Electronically Via Interfolio:

Cover letter detailing qualifications related to the position description.
Curriculum Vitae.
Statement of teaching philosophy that includes a brief description of past teaching experience, no more than two pages.
Research Statement that details current and future environmental science research, no more than two pages.
Statement of leadership philosophy that includes a brief description of administrative and leadership experiences as they relate to Program Director-level service, no more than one page.
Contact information for three professional references. Letters will be requested from short-listed candidates.

Inquiries may be directed to Richelle Tanner, Search Committee Chair, at schmidcollege@chapman.edu. Please use "Environmental Science & Policy Faculty Position" as the email subject line.

Application review will begin October 11, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled. This position is subject to final budget approval. Salary range for this position is $105,000 - $125,000. Successful completion of a background check is required for the final candidate.

jobs.description:
The Agency You’ll Join

The New York City Mayor’s Office is responsible for overseeing city services throughout the five boroughs, coordinating public agencies and departments, and managing public property. The administration is leading the fight in making the city more affordable, reducing inequality, improving public safety, ensuring delivery of efficient and effective services, and working to make New York City’s economy stronger. We value leadership, transparency, fairness, and efficiency as we actively seek diverse talents from various sectors to join our team. For current job opportunities, visit our careers page.

The Team You’ll Work With

The Office of the Deputy Mayor for Economic Justice advances policies that promote a more equitable and vibrant New York City. The portfolio includes the City's economic, cultural, and workforce agencies and offices.

The Mayor's Office of Worker Power (MOWP) is a new office within the Office of the Deputy Mayor for Economic Justice focused on using the tools and platform of City government to build worker power. MOWP works with workers, unions, worker centers, community organizations, and City agencies to support worker organizing and campaigns, develop policies that strengthen workers' rights and power, and ensure workers have a meaningful voice in City government.

The Deputy Director/Senior Advisor reports to the Director of the Office of Worker Power and helps run the day-to-day work of the office, translating the Director's vision and external relationships into operations, staffing, and follow-through

The Problems You’ll Solve

Help shape strategy alongside the Director and the broader DMEJ team, connecting MOWP's work to the office's wider priorities.

Support organizing campaigns and partnerships with unions, worker centers, and community organizations, particularly in industries with low union density and significant worker exploitation.

Draft policy proposals and legislative language that strengthen worker power, working closely with legal and policy staff.

Coordinate with City agencies to implement worker power initiatives and track their progress.

Monitor emerging workplace issues, including the impact of AI, algorithms, and other economic changes, and prepare briefings and recommendations for the Director.

Help plan and staff public meetings and hearings on significant worker issues.

Oversee research and data efforts tracking wage growth, workforce equity, union density, and other measures of worker power.

Serve as a key point of contact for the office and represent MOWP in the Director's absence.

About You

You have organizing experience and a track record of contributing to winning campaigns on behalf of workers.
You have a strong understanding of the NYC and national labor movement, including its challenges, opportunities, and different constituencies.
You have experience managing people, projects, or programs, and turning strategy into an executable workplan.
You have strong working relationships and credibility with workers, unions, worker organizations, and other key stakeholders.

Minimum Required Qualifications

7+ years of experience in the labor movement, including at a union, worker center, or organization that directly represents workers; NYC experience strongly preferred.
Organizing experience and a track record of contributing to winning campaigns on behalf of workers.
Strong understanding of the NYC and national labor movement, including its challenges, opportunities, and different constituencies.
Experience managing people, projects, or programs, and turning strategy into an executable workplan.
Strong working relationships and credibility with workers, unions, worker organizations, and other key stakeholders.

Preferred Skills

Experience drafting policy proposals or legislative language.
Experience managing a team, office, or complex project with multiple moving pieces.
Familiarity with NYC government structure and how City agencies operate.
Experience using research and data to track labor market or workforce trends.

Do you have an associate degree from an accredited college or university along with two (2) years of experience with administrative, analytic, coordinative, supervisory or liaison responsibilities?

jobs.description:

The Business Development Director will lead business development strategy and execution, working closely with practice leadership and lawyers across the firm to drive growth, strengthen client relationships, identify new business opportunities, and expand the practice’s capabilities across practices and geographies.

Serving as a strategic advisor to Investment Management leadership, you’ll bring a strong understanding of the investment management industry, its clients, competitive dynamics, and evolving market and regulatory environment. You’ll translate market, client, and firm insights into actionable opportunities and drive strategic initiatives from concept through execution.

You’ll collaborate with Business Development, Marketing, and other firm functions to advance client targeting, cross-practice and cross-office collaboration, thought leadership, and market visibility. You’ll also help drive the strategic priorities and operating rhythm of the practice while overseeing a team of Business Development professionals.

Maintaining an in-office presence is important to delivering our services through an integrated and collaborative work culture. This position can
be resident in any one of our Boston,
New York, Philadelphia, or Washington, DC offices

.

What You’ll Do

Lead business development for the Investment Management practice, partnering with practice leadership to establish growth priorities and execute plans aligned with firm objectives.
Serve as a strategic advisor to practice leadership and lawyers on client development, market positioning, competitive differentiation, and growth opportunities.
Develop a deep understanding of the practice’s clients, capabilities, competitive position, and priority markets and lead targeting and relationship-development initiatives that grow existing relationships, develop new clients, and expand work across practices and geographies.
Monitor investment management industry developments and analyze client, financial, pipeline, matter, and market data to identify opportunities and translate insights into actionable business development and go-to-market strategies.

Lead and develop a team of Business Development professionals, setting priorities, allocating workloads, providing coaching and feedback, evaluating performance, and fostering a collaborative, high-performing team.

What Sets This Role Apart

Strategic Impact: Serve as a strategic advisor to Investment Management leadership and help shape growth priorities for a sophisticated, global practice.
Industry Focus: Apply your knowledge of the investment management industry, client needs, competitive dynamics, and market developments to identify and advance meaningful opportunities.
Leadership & Collaboration: Lead and develop a Business Development team while partnering with practice leaders, lawyers, and colleagues across practices, offices, and firm functions.
Market & Client Engagement: Help strengthen key client relationships and advance the practice’s market position through targeted business development, thought leadership, and cross-firm collaboration.

This role offers a hybrid three (3) days per week in-office schedule in our Boston, New York, Philadelphia, or Washington, DC office providing flexibility while supporting our collaborative, team-based culture.

Experience working with investment management, asset management, private funds, financial services, or related industries strongly preferred; law firm or other professional-services experience preferred.

Strong strategic and commercial orientation, with the ability to synthesize market, client, competitive, financial, legal, and regulatory information and translate insights into practical recommendations and opportunities.
Proven success building credibility with, advising, and influencing senior leaders and professionals in a collaborative, highly matrixed environment.
Demonstrated leadership and people-management skills, including setting priorities, developing talent, providing effective feedback, and leading through direct management and influence.
Excellent planning, organizational, analytical, and project-management skills, with a track record of moving complex initiatives from strategy through execution while managing competing priorities.
Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and executive communication skills, along with strong interpersonal skills and a client-service orientation.

Chapman University invites applications for an Associate or Full Professor of Environmental Science & Policy and Program Director in the Schmid College of Science and Technology starting August 2027. Dedicated to forward-looking, personalized education, we create an environment for unlimited achievement by both our students and faculty. More information about Chapman University is available at www.chapman.edu.

The Environmental Science & Policy Program is uniquely seated within two colleges at Chapman University: the Schmid College of Science and Technology and the Wilkinson College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences. Schmid and Wilkinson Colleges embody Chapman's mission of providing students with personalized educational experiences by fostering an outstanding community of teacher-scholars across a broad range of undergraduate and graduate programs. , respectively.

Environmental health
Environmental toxicology
Water, soil, and/or air quality
Environmental contaminants
Natural resource governance

The successful candidate will teach lower- and upper-level courses that contribute to the major and minors within the Environmental Science & Policy Program, maintain an active research program, and advise/mentor undergraduate research students. Lead curriculum alignment and revisions, assessment reports, and course scheduling for the program.

Assign faculty to courses and hire appropriate part-time lecturers where needed.
Facilitate communication and collaboration between Schmid and Wilkinson Colleges pertaining to the support of this interdisciplinary program.

The company primarily provides services in electrical installation, preventive maintenance, communications and data center infrastructure, EV charging facilities, renewable energy, energy efficiency, lighting, gas systems, HVAC, and fire detection systems.
With a professional team of approximately 250 employees, the company is dedicated to providing customized, energy-efficient, and sustainable engineering solutions to both corporate and individual clients.
Official Website: [https://montegar.es/](https://montegar.es/)
## Position Overview
The Chief Operating Officer (COO) will be responsible for establishing, developing, and managing the day-to-day operations of the US business. This role involves building local management systems and overseeing engineering projects, financial performance, supply chain, quality, safety, and regulatory compliance.
Key Responsibilities
Lead the establishment and daily operations of the US business.
Develop and implement operational strategies, annual budgets, and performance targets.
Build and manage teams across engineering, project management, procurement, finance, and customer service.
Oversee projects related to electrical systems, data centers, charging infrastructure, and renewable energy.
Manage project costs, schedules, quality, and delivery performance.
Establish relationships with suppliers, contractors, and technical partners.
Refine management systems for occupational health, safety, environment, and quality (HSEQ).
Ensure business compliance with US federal, state, and local regulations.
Identify and mitigate risks related to projects, supply chain, finance, and operations.
Report operational results regularly to the CEO and the Board of Directors.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree or higher in Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
12+ years of operational experience in engineering, energy, construction, or infrastructure sectors.
5+ years of experience in senior management and leading cross-functional teams.
Experience with electrical engineering, data centers, renewable energy, or large-scale projects.
Proficiency in budgeting, procurement, contract management, supply chain, and project cost management.
Familiarity with US engineering permitting, safety, and environmental regulations is preferred.
Strong capabilities in strategic planning, negotiation, and organizational development.
Fluent in English; proficiency in Spanish is a plus. Benefits
